title: Generalized linear models and Fisher scoring

items.title: Explicit exponential-family response contracts
items.statement: For a finite independent response vector, specify its component densities or masses, sigma-finite base measures, common supports, dispersion factors, and product sampling law.
items.strategy: Definition: give the normalized component laws and their finite product; state support and differentiability conventions.

items.title: Mean and variance from the cumulant function
items.statement: Under common support, twice differentiable densities, local integrable derivative envelopes, and finite second moments, the displayed one-parameter family has mean b'(theta) and variance a(phi)b''(theta).
items.strategy: Differentiate the normalized density integral once and twice, with the mean value theorem and dominated convergence justifying both interchanges.

items.title: The product response law has the product density
items.statement:
In the setup of [[def-glm-observation-family]], let $P_\theta=\bigotimes_{i=1}^nP_{i,\theta_i,\phi}$ and $\nu=\bigotimes_{i=1}^n\nu_i$. Then the joint sampling law has density

$$q_\theta(y_1,\ldots,y_n)=\prod_{i=1}^n f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)$$

relative to $\nu$. At any $y$ for which every factor $f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)$ is positive, the log likelihood is $\log q_\theta(y)=\sum_i\log f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)$.
items.strategy: Prove measurability, use Tonelli on rectangles and total mass, then apply finite-measure uniqueness on the generating rectangle pi-system.

items.title: Generalized linear model with explicit conditioning
items.statement:
Fix $n\ge1$, $p\ge1$, a finite design matrix $X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}$ with rows $x_i^\mathsf T$, a dispersion value $\phi$, and an open parameter domain $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$. A **generalized linear model (GLM)** on this design consists of the response family in [[def-glm-observation-family]], a differentiable one-to-one link $g:\mathcal M\to g(\mathcal M)$ on a specified mean domain $\mathcal M$, and a specified map $\tau:\mathcal M\to J$ satisfying $b'(\tau(\mu))=\mu$. For $\beta\in\Theta$, put

$$\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta,\qquad \mu_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i),\qquad \theta_i=\tau(\mu_i),$$

and require $\eta_i\in g(\mathcal M)$ and $\theta_i\in J$ for every $i$. The **canonical link** is the choice $g=\tau$, equivalently $\theta_i=\eta_i$. When $\theta_i=\eta_i$ and the component scales are common, write $a_i(\phi)=a(\phi)>0$; this common-scale restriction is part of every formula that uses $a(\phi)$.

The joint sampling density is the product density from [[lem-glm-product-density]]. For an observed $y=(y_1,\ldots,y_n)$ with $f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)>0$ for every $i$, define its log likelihood by

$$\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=\sum_{i=1}^n\left\{\frac{y_i\theta_i-b(\theta_i)}{a_i(\phi)}+c_i(y_i,\phi)\right\}.$$

For a differentiable log likelihood, the **score** is $U(\beta;y,\phi):=\nabla_\beta\ell(\beta;y,\phi)$. When its entries have finite second moments, the **expected score outer-product information** is $I(\beta,\phi):=\mathbb E_{\beta,\phi}[U U^\mathsf T]$. This page treats $X$ as fixed or conditions on its realized value; it supplies no random-design asymptotic conclusion.
items.strategy: Definition: specify the parameter domain, the fixed or conditioned design, common-scale convention, response family, link, likelihood, score, and information.

items.title: Likelihood deviance for nested models on common support
items.statement:
Fix an observed response vector $y$ for which the component densities are positive throughout both models' parameter sets, and two stated GLMs with the same response family, base support, and log-likelihood function $\ell(\beta;y)$. They are **nested** here only when a stated embedding identifies the fitted parameter set with a subset $\Theta_{\mathrm{fit}}\subseteq\Theta_{\mathrm{sat}}$ of the saturated reference parameter set. Require both sets to be nonempty and both suprema to be finite real numbers. The **likelihood deviance** is

$$D(y)=2\left\{\sup_{\beta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{sat}}}\ell(\beta;y)-\sup_{\beta\in\Theta_{\mathrm{fit}}}\ell(\beta;y)\right\}.$$

The definition makes no claim about deviance residuals, goodness-of-fit diagnostics, or a reference distribution. The two full-text GLM notes cited above support likelihood setup but do not supply a deviance-diagnostics treatment; the nonnegativity result below is proved only from the stated set inclusion.
items.strategy: Definition only; residual diagnostics and reference distributions are outside scope.

items.title: Canonical-link score and Hessian
items.statement:
Let $(Y_i)_{i=1}^n$ follow [[def-generalized-linear-model]] with a common scale $a(\phi)>0$, canonical link $\theta_i=\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta$, and twice differentiable $b$. For an observed $y$ with $f_i(y_i;\eta_i,\phi)>0$ for every $i$,

$$\nabla_\beta\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=\frac{X^\mathsf T(y-\mu)}{a(\phi)},\qquad \nabla_\beta^2\ell(\beta;y,\phi)=-\frac{X^\mathsf T\operatorname{diag}(b''(\eta_i))X}{a(\phi)}.$$
items.strategy: Differentiate the product log likelihood coordinatewise and assemble the gradient and Hessian using the stated matrix differential rules.

items.title: General-link score and Fisher information
items.statement:
Consider [[def-generalized-linear-model]] at an admissible finite $\beta$ with common scale $a(\phi)>0$. Assume each $\eta_i\mapsto\theta_i$ is differentiable, each $\eta_i\mapsto\mu_i$ is differentiable with $\dot\mu_i:=d\mu_i/d\eta_i\ne0$, $V_i:=b''(\theta_i)>0$, the component scores have finite second moments, and the common-support, differentiability, and local integrable derivative-envelope conditions from [[def-glm-observation-family]] hold. Put

$$w_i=\frac{\dot\mu_i^2}{a(\phi)V_i},\qquad z_i=\eta_i+\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\dot\mu_i}.$$

For every observed $y$ with $f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)>0$ for each $i$, the score and expected score outer-product information are

$$U(\beta;y,\phi)=X^\mathsf T\left(\frac{\dot\mu_i(y_i-\mu_i)}{a(\phi)V_i}\right)_{i=1}^n,\qquad I(\beta,\phi)=X^\mathsf T\operatorname{diag}(w_i)X.$$

In particular, if $X$ has full column rank, then $I$ is positive definite.
items.strategy: Apply the chain rule through theta=(b')^{-1}(mu), then compute the score second moment from the component means, variances, and independence.

items.title: One minimum-norm IRLS step
items.statement:
Inputs are an observed response vector $y$ with $f_i(y_i;\theta_i,\phi)>0$ for every $i$, a finite design matrix $X$, an admissible finite current parameter $\beta$, and a GLM with common scale $a(\phi)>0$. Require each $\dot\mu_i=d\mu_i/d\eta_i$ to be finite and nonzero and each $V_i=b''(\theta_i)$ to be finite and positive.

1. Compute $\eta_i=x_i^\mathsf T\beta$ and $\mu_i=g^{-1}(\eta_i)$.
2. Compute the **working response** and positive weight
$$z_i=\eta_i+\frac{y_i-\mu_i}{\dot\mu_i},\qquad w_i=\frac{\dot\mu_i^2}{a(\phi)V_i}.$$
3. Form $W^{1/2}=\operatorname{diag}(\sqrt{w_i})$ using [[thm-of-square-roots]], and put $A=W^{1/2}X$, $r=W^{1/2}z$. By [[def-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse]] and [[thm-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse-exists-and-is-unique]], form $A^+$. Return $\beta_{\mathrm{new}}=A^+r$, the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm member of the nonempty weighted least-squares minimizer set by [[thm-a-plus-b-is-the-unique-minimum-norm-least-squares-solution]].

The Moore--Penrose convention makes the procedure single-valued even when $X$ is rank deficient; the underlying least-squares minimizer need not then be unique. Existence and the minimum-norm property follow from [[thm-moore-penrose-pseudoinverse-exists-and-is-unique]] and [[thm-a-plus-b-is-the-unique-minimum-norm-least-squares-solution]]. The output need not lie in $\Theta$, and this definition makes no claim that repeated updates terminate or converge to a maximizer.
items.strategy: Define a single-valued minimum-norm generalized-inverse convention; no termination, convergence, or MLE-existence property is claimed.

items.title: The minimum-norm IRLS step is well-defined for every design rank
items.axiom_use: This is a finite real-matrix specialization of the stated suppliers; it introduces no choice among minimizers and no additional choice assumption.

references.title: Stanford CS205L, Unit 11: Zero Singular Values, Moore–Penrose least-squares selection
Ryan Tibshirani, Generalized Linear Models, CMU Advanced Methods for Data Analysis, Fisher scoring and weighted least squares

items.statement:
For every input satisfying the Definition of [[alg-fisher-scoring-irls]], every intermediate quantity in its three instructions is uniquely determined and finite. Its output $\beta_{\mathrm{new}}\in\mathbb R^p$ is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm member of the nonempty set
$$\operatorname*{argmin}_{\gamma\in\mathbb R^p}\sum_{i=1}^n w_i(z_i-x_i^\mathsf T\gamma)^2.$$
This holds for every rank of $X$, including $X=0$. The weighted normal matrix $H=X^\mathsf T W X$ is positive semidefinite and has kernel $\ker H=\ker X$; its singularity does not obstruct this output. No assertion that the output lies in the model parameter domain, or that repeated updates converge, is made.

items.title: Nested-model deviance is nonnegative
items.statement: For the finite-supremum deviance definition, inclusion of the fitted model in the saturated model implies D>=0.
items.strategy: Compare the suprema over nested parameter sets and multiply the resulting inequality by two.

items.title: Strict concavity and uniqueness of a finite stationary maximizer
items.statement: Suppose the canonical-link GLM has an open convex parameter domain $\Theta\subseteq\mathbb R^p$, full-column-rank design $X$, common scale $a(\phi)>0$, and $b''(\eta_i)>0$ at every predictor vector in $X\Theta$. For a fixed response vector $y$ whose component densities are positive throughout $\Theta$, $\ell(\,\cdot\,;y,\phi)$ is strictly concave on $\Theta$. It has at most one stationary point; if a stationary point exists, it is the unique global maximizer. This conclusion does not assert that a finite maximizer exists.
items.strategy: Restrict the log likelihood to each nonconstant line and use its strictly negative second derivative; use the mean value theorem to compare values.

items.title: IRLS equals the Fisher-scoring step when information is invertible
items.statement:
Under the admissibility hypotheses of [[alg-fisher-scoring-irls]], assume also that each map $\eta_i\mapsto\theta_i$ is differentiable, each map $\eta_i\mapsto\mu_i$ is differentiable with finite nonzero derivative $\dot\mu_i$, and $V_i:=b''(\theta_i)>0$. Each response has finite second moment, its density has the fixed common support and locally uniform integrable envelopes for its first and second $\theta_i$ derivatives required by [[def-glm-observation-family]], and each component score has finite second moment. If $I(\beta)=X^\mathsf T W X$ is invertible, let $U(\beta)$ and $I(\beta)$ be the score and expected score outer-product information from [[thm-glm-general-link-score-and-information]]. Then the weighted least-squares output satisfies

$$\beta_{\mathrm{new}}=\beta+I(\beta)^{-1}U(\beta).$$
items.strategy: Rewrite the weighted response residual as the score contribution and apply the weighted least-squares normal equation.

title: Generalized linear models and Fisher scoring — Examples

items.title: A mean-matched count law can be overdispersed relative to Poisson
items.statement: The law assigning probability one half to 0 and one half to 20 has mean 10 and variance 100, so it shares a Poisson(10) mean but not its variance 10.
items.strategy: Compute the two moments and compare them with the Poisson variance identity.

items.title: The Bernoulli identity-link boundary leaves the regular family
items.statement: For a Bernoulli identity-link model, the boundary mean mu=0 is outside the finite natural-parameter interior and the Fisher-scoring weight 1/(mu(1-mu)) diverges as mu decreases to 0.
items.strategy: Use the Bernoulli variance function and the nonzero identity-link derivative to compute the weight and identify the excluded boundary.

items.title: Complete separation prevents a finite logistic MLE
items.statement: For x=(-1,1) and y=(0,1), the logistic log likelihood is strictly increasing on every finite beta and approaches its supremum only as beta tends to positive infinity.
items.strategy: Write the two Bernoulli likelihood factors, differentiate the log likelihood, and compute the limiting supremum.

items.title: Rank deficiency gives singular information and nonunique weighted least squares
items.statement: For the two-column design with rows (1,1) and (2,2), Bernoulli-logit beta=0, and responses (0,1), the information matrix is singular and the weighted least-squares minimizers form a line; the Moore-Penrose convention selects one member.
items.strategy: Compute the positive weights, the rank-one information matrix, and the objective as a function of beta_1+beta_2.

items.title: A one-observation Bernoulli-logit Fisher-scoring step
items.statement: For y=x=1 and beta=0, the Bernoulli-logit score is 1/2, information and weight are 1/4, working response is 2, and both IRLS and Fisher scoring return beta+=2.
items.strategy: Compute the Bernoulli cumulant, mean, variance, score, information, working response, and weighted least-squares minimizer explicitly.

items.title: A one-observation Poisson-log Fisher-scoring step
items.statement: For y=2, x=1 and beta=0, the Poisson-log score, information and weight are 1, the working response is 1, and both IRLS and Fisher scoring return beta+=1.
items.strategy: Use b(theta)=exp(theta), evaluate the score and information, and solve the one-dimensional weighted least-squares problem.
